deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 114–116). The page belongs to an exposition of the correspondence between linear substitutions and bilinear forms, in the style of Frobenius 1878. It probably comes from lecture notes; the preceding text on p. 114 is an unrelated invariant-theory argument.

Setup from p. 114: a general binary substitution S: x1' = a11 x1 + a12 x2, x2' = a21 x1 + a22 x2. In matrix form x' = A x with A = (alpha_ik). Its associated bilinear form is phi = u1(a11 x1 + a12 x2) + u2(a21 x1 + a22 x2) = u^T A x.

Step 1 (this page). After S, a second substitution T is applied: x'' = B x' with B = (beta_ik). The product, written ST (meaning first S, then T), is x'' = B A x. Hilbert writes out only the first coefficient: x1'' = (alpha11 beta11 + beta12 alpha21) x1 + ... . This is the (1,1) entry of BA. The remaining entries are left as dashes. My completion: x1'' = (b11 a11 + b12 a21) x1 + (b11 a12 + b12 a22) x2 and x2'' = (b21 a11 + b22 a21) x1 + (b21 a12 + b22 a22) x2.

Step 2. A Fraktur letter (B, later K) denotes the map 'substitution -> its bilinear form'. So B(S) = phi = u^T A x.

Step 3. For the transformed substitution T S T^{-1}, the form is written in new variables omega (contravariant) and xi (covariant): B(TST^{-1}) = sum_{i,k} a_ik omega_i xi_k = x1'' omega1 + x2'' omega2. Here x'' is to be expressed in xi, and (p. 116) xi = B x. Since x = B^{-1} xi, we get x'' = B A x = (B A B^{-1}) xi. So (a_ik) = B A B^{-1}, and the page's T S T^{-1} must be read as the matrix product B A B^{-1}.

Step 4 (completed on p. 116). How is B(TST^{-1}) obtained from B(S)? Compute omega^T x'' = omega^T B A x = (B^T omega)^T A x. Hence B(TST^{-1}) arises from B(S) = u^T A x by the substitutions x -> B^{-1} xi (i.e. xi = Bx) and u = B^T omega, i.e. u1 = b11 w1 + b21 w2, u2 = b12 w1 + b22 w2. These are exactly the formulas on p. 116.

Purpose. Conjugating (similarity-transforming) a substitution corresponds to transforming its bilinear form by a cogredient/contragredient pair of substitutions. This is the basis for classifying substitutions up to similarity via bilinear forms (Weierstrass–Kronecker–Frobenius elementary divisors).
errors: Composition-order notation is not consistent. 'ST' is used for 'first S then T' (matrix BA). Under that left-to-right convention, the matrix B A B^{-1} computed for 'TST^{-1}' would be written T^{-1} S T. The label TST^{-1} matches the right-to-left (matrix-product) convention instead. The mathematics is correct once B A B^{-1} is understood.
The coefficients a_ik on this page are not defined. Implicitly they are the entries of B A B^{-1}.
The product ST is left mostly unwritten (dashes). The one written coefficient, alpha11 beta11 + beta12 alpha21, is correct.
Next page (transcription): '(beta21 x1' + beta2 x2'')' should read beta22 x2'. This is a slip in the manuscript or in the transcription.

results.what: Composition of two binary linear substitutions corresponds to matrix multiplication (coefficient of x1 in x1'' is b11 a11 + b12 a21)
results.modern_name: matrix product / composition of linear maps

results.what: Correspondence substitution <-> bilinear form u^T A x, with the conjugate substitution B A B^{-1} corresponding to the form transformed by xi = Bx and u = B^T omega (contragredient transformation)
results.modern_name: similarity transformation of a matrix vs. cogredient/contragredient transformation of a bilinear form (Frobenius' symbolic calculus of bilinear forms)
results.usually_credited_to: Frobenius 1878 ('Über lineare Substitutionen und bilineare Formen'); Weierstrass 1868, Kronecker

deep.surprise_reason: This is textbook material from Frobenius' 1878 theory of substitutions and bilinear forms, apparently written as lecture or study notes. Nothing here is original or non-standard.

checkable.asserts: Coefficient of x1 in x1'' for 'first S then T' is alpha11*beta11 + beta12*alpha21

checkable.sympy: x1,x2,w1,w2=symbols('x1 x2 w1 w2'); x=Matrix([x1,x2]); w=Matrix([w1,w2]); xi=B*x; u=B.T*w; simplify((w.T*(B*A*B.inv())*xi)[0]-(u.T*A*x)[0])==0
checkable.asserts: The form of B A B^{-1} in (omega, xi) with xi = Bx equals the form of S, u^T A x, under u = B^T omega
B(TST^{-1}) = x1''*omega1 + x2''*omega2 with x'' = B A x
u1 = beta11 w1 + beta21 w2 and u2 = beta12 w1 + beta22 w2 (formulas on p. 116)

transcription_corrections: The crossed-out words before 'so entsteht' are most likely 'auf S an' (continuing 'Wende ich nun die Substitution S an' from p. 114), not 'auf Sau'.
The Fraktur symbol rendered \mathfrak{B} (stands for 'Bilinearform') appears as K on the next page; the same letter is meant throughout.
On the ST line, x1 is unprimed as written ('x_1 +'), which is consistent with x'' expressed in the original variables.
